extracted.intended_audience: aspiring authors, journalists, and literary students
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and evaluative principles for early-career authors and journalists on style, study, editorial conduct, and the intellectual aims of writing. Covers methods for historical/political analysis, measures of scholarly usefulness, and study practices to develop literary taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct a paper on fixed, announced principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper should thenceforwards be conducted on certain fixed and announced principles, and that I should neither be obliged nor requested to deviate from them in favour of any party or any event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial independence: set and publish a code of principles for the journal and refuse pressure to depart from them; use this as the foundation of the paper's political stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality defined
rubrics_metrics.description: By impartiality I mean an honest and enlightened adherence to a code of intelligible principles previously announced, and faithfully referred to in support of every judgment on men and events; not indiscriminate abuse, not the indulgence of an editor’s own malignant passions, and still less ... a determination to make money by flattering the envy and cupidity, the vindictive restlessness and self-conceit of the half-witted vulgar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impartiality is active adherence to announced principles plus restraint from personal malice or pandering to popular vice; anti-patterns include indiscriminate abuse, personal spite, and pandering for profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper success: impartiality plus literary talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Genuine impartiality with a respectable portion of literary talent will secure the success of a newspaper without the aid of party or ministerial patronage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metric of success: circulation and influence can follow from principled impartiality combined with real literary ability rather than from partisan backing or patronage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use historical analogy methodically
rubrics_metrics.description: On every great occurrence I endeavoured to discover in past history the event, that most nearly resembled it ... Then fairly subtracting the points of difference from those of likeness ... I conjectured that the result would be the same or different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: identify the closest historical parallel, collect contemporary and original documents, subtract differences from likenesses, and infer whether outcomes will be analogous; avoid superficial or emotive comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground political judgment in history and human nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Armed with the two-fold knowledge of history and the human mind, a man will scarcely err in his judgment concerning the sum total of any future national event, if he have been able to procure the original documents of the past, together with authentic accounts of the present, and if he have a philosophic tact for what is truly important in facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements for reliable forecasting: substantive historical knowledge, understanding of human psychology, original primary sources, trustworthy current accounts, and the ability to discern which facts matter (including facts often omitted by standard histories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure a scholar's utility by influence and truths circulated
rubrics_metrics.description: The criterion of a scholar’s utility [should be] the number and moral value of the truths, which he has been the means of throwing into the general circulation; or the number and value of the minds, whom by his conversation or letters, he has excited into activity, and supplied with the germs of their after-growth!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject counting publications as the sole measure; value the moral significance of ideas disseminated and the intellectual influence a scholar exerts through teaching, conversation, and correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stylistic excesses that impede readers
rubrics_metrics.description: My prose writings have been charged with a disproportionate demand on the attention; with an excess of refinement in the mode of arriving at truths; with beating the ground for that which might have been run down by the eye; with the length and laborious construction of my periods; in short with obscurity and the love of paradox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These listed faults serve as negative criteria: good prose should not demand disproportionate attention, be over-refined in method, needlessly repetitive, excessively long-perioded, obscure, or fond of paradox for its own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquire grounded knowledge via original texts and language study
rubrics_metrics.description: My chief efforts were directed towards a grounded knowledge of the German language and literature ... I read with sedulous accuracy the Minnesinger ... laboured through sufficient specimens of the master singers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical study advice for authors: learn relevant languages, attend lectures, study grammar and original texts closely and painstakingly to develop a genuine tact for style and to understand literary tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define political terms precisely to prevent misuse
rubrics_metrics.description: In distinguishing the Jacobin from the republican, the democrat, and the mere demagogue, I both rescued the word from remaining a mere term of abuse, and put on their guard many honest minds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical precision: carefully define and distinguish terms so that they carry specific meanings rather than functioning as vague insults; this clarity protects honest readers and improves argumentative rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame current events in moral and principle-based terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Placing the questions and events of the day in a moral point of view; in giving a dignity to particular measures by tracing their policy or impolicy to permanent principles, and an interest to principles by the application of them to individual measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principled critique: increase the dignity and relevance of commentary by linking policies and events to enduring moral or political principles and by using specific measures to illustrate broader principles.
